newsitem.title: USA: U.S. average retail beef prices rise in month - NCBA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. average retail beef prices rise in month - NCBA.

text.p: Average retail beef prices rose slightly during the past month, the National Cattlemen's Beef Association (NCBA) said in a report.

The NCBA, summarizing its regular monthly 19-city survey of supermarkets, said the average price of six cuts of beef on November 14 was $3.04 per lb, compared with $3.02 on October 10 and $2.98 a year ago.

It said beef production remained limited in recent weeks and cattle and wholesale beef prices were at some of their highest levels in more than a year. Retailers continued to actively feature beef at special low prices.
The NCBA six-cut average on Nov 14 was up from a month earlier in 12 cities but was down in seven.

The 19-city averages for the six cuts on Nov 14 were as follows: regular ground beef, $1.48 per lb; lean ground beef, $1.89; boneless round steak, $2.95; boneless top sirloin steak, $3.86; T-bone steak, $5.66; and boneless chuck roll roast $2.41.
